scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You type a question, and in half a second, Google shows you the answer from billions of pages. How?

scenes.name: crawl
scenes.text: Long before you search, programs called crawlers visit web pages, and follow every link to find new ones.

scenes.name: index
scenes.text: What they find is stored in a giant index, like the index at the back of a book. Each word points to the pages that use it.

scenes.name: understand
scenes.text: When you search, it first works out what you mean. It fixes spelling, and understands synonyms and context.

scenes.name: match
scenes.text: Then it looks up the index, and pulls out the pages that match, without reading the whole web again.

scenes.name: rank
scenes.text: Hundreds of signals rank them. Relevance, quality, freshness, your location, and how useful the page has been to others.

scenes.name: serve
scenes.text: All this runs on huge data centres, split across many machines at once. That's how it fits into half a second.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Crawl, index, understand, rank. A library at your fingertips. Follow for more on how things really work.
